picks.reasoning: Individual skill wins series, and HLE's mid laner Zeka is the kind of player who decides a single game while TES has no one who matches that. LCK sits above LPL on the international stage, and I'm not letting a flashy comeback streak talk me out of that.

Tempo is what decides this, and HLE own the first 15 minutes: they take towers and dragons, and they keep the map even when they give up the first kill. TES still get the early skirmishes, but they don't turn them into objectives, and LCK is the stronger region here, so HLE get the benefit of the doubt once the lanes start moving.

Under Fearless, the side that keeps its mid pool deep wins the draft, and Zeka's Orianna, Syndra, and Ahri give HLE three answers to whatever TES forces, while Ryze-heavy TES gets squeezed once the bans start. LCK's clear edge in this matchup means HLE gets the benefit of the doubt in a single game.

The LCK-LPL gap is the biggest number on this sheet: LCK has taken 15-7 against other regions to LPL's 9-5, and HLE's 30-14 series mark beats TES's 27-24. HLE's 2-4 record against LPL this year keeps this from being a lock, but the international results give me enough to lean HLE.

Team chemistry and mood are what I trust most, and HLE's group looks like it knows how to close out a lead, even if their comeback record is thin. The LCK gap is too big to wave away, so I'm backing the side that's been more composed when it matters, with TES needing a swing to get back into it.
